Vega plea for Scottish FA backing against Infantino - gossip
1 of 2
- Published
Former Celtic centre-half Ramon Vega urges the Scottish FA to support his bid to oust Fifa president Gianni Infantino as Stephen Robinson admits he has no funds to add free agents to Aberdeen's squad.
Former Celtic centre-half Ramon Vega has already reached out to the Scottish FA to support his bid to oust the controversial Gianni Infantino as president of world governing body Fifa. (The Herald, external)
Friday's win over Coventry City marked David Moyes' 592nd game in charge of Everton across two spells, equalling legendary boss Harry Catterick's record, and the Scot will set a new mark when they travel to Brentford after the international break. (TalkSport, external)
Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson has confirmed he has no budget to raid the free agent market for reinforcements amid a defensive injury crisis. (Press & Journal, external)
Calvin Ramsay has no regrets about swapping regular games with Aberdeen for fleeting appearances with Liverpool before the 23-year-old right-back's current loan to St Mirren. (Scottish Sun, external)
Midfielder Findlay Marshall says being told his Aberdeen career was coming to an end by previous manager Jimmy Thelin delivered "the jolt I needed". (Press & Journal, external)

Rangers still have high hopes for midfielder Vanja Dragojevic despite the 20-year-old big-money summer signing from Partizan Belgrade barely being seen since the Europa League defeat by Jablonec in early August. (Daily Record, external)
Scotland centre-half Grant Hanley will miss Hibernian's visit to Aberdeen on Saturday after undergoing an operation on an injured thumb. (Edinburgh Evening News, external)
Brondby head coach Thomas Norgaard has insisted Luis Binks will be fit to play against FC Copenhagen - and for Scotland - despite the centre-half hobbling off on his return from injury. (The National, external)
St Johnstone manager Simo Valakari says Danny Schmidt is likely to miss Saturday's game against Dundee with an ankle injury the midfielder played through against Kilmarnock. (The Courier, external)
Matthew Gillies on Friday did not know whether he would be playing against Falkirk on Sunday or for Stenhousemuir on Saturday after the 19-year-old midfielder was recalled from his loan to make his debut for injury hit Heart of Midlothian against Thun on Thursday. (Daily Record, external)
A fresh public consultation is to be held on Dundee's plans for a new stadium as the wait for a decision goes on. (The Courier, external)
